Over the last year, I've purchased 30+ laptops for work. Not an expert, but I've seen a larger sample size than most.

  1. All modern laptops are under powered and under cooled. This is the 'apple factor'.
  2. The specs you can see (e.g. memory capacity) are good, the specs you can't see (e.g. memory speed) are terrible. They intentionally cut corners on non headline specs.
  3. Asus is probably the best of the worst. They were a standout winner 5-7 years ago, but in the last ~2 years, the have been forced to race to the bottom on the cost front. I'd still recommend Asus over most other brands. I wouldn't touch HP, Dell, Acer even if you gave it to me.

My general recommendation that I give most people: Get 2 machines. Trying to do 'everything' in a portable form factor results in too much compromise on cooling, power, etc.

  1. Build your own desktop. pcpartpicker.com The manufacturers put their 'good stuff' in the product lines that they sell to enthusiasts. (E.g. an Asus motherboard sold alone will typically be far better than an Asus motherboard that is sold as part of a complete system.) This machine becomes your heavy lifter for productivity, games, rendering, editing, etc. If you can't / won't build your own system, then just get a desktop PC. At least here you will have enough cooling for the components to run as originally designed.
  2. Get a light weight chromebook. As long as you can use google docs / sheets / etc, you will be highly satisfied with a light weight / long battery life / robust mobile system.
